papers.title_in_file: Recruit Communications: Applying Quantum Computing to Digital Marketing (CASE STORY)
papers.what_it_is: A two-page D-Wave Systems marketing case story (2021) describing Recruit Communications projects on TV ad allocation, feature selection and hotel search ranking using D-Wave quantum annealing.

assertions.value: The paper states that in 2017 Recruit announced a first-of-its-kind collaboration with D-Wave aimed at optimizing marketing, advertising, and communications technologies and strategies.
assertions.anchor: Section 'Right User, Right Time, Right Message', p.1
quotes: In 2017, they announced a first-of-its-kind collaboration with D-Wave aimed at optimizing marketing, advertising, and communications technologies and strategies.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of its own collaboration; no evidence given.

assertions.value: The paper states the TV advertising problem: the goal is to reach individual viewers enough times to push them over a tipping point, called the Minimum Effective Frequency (MEF), past which brand recognition increases suddenly and dramatically; Recruit sought to identify and reach the maximum number of viewers who could be nurtured to the MEF point within the budget.
assertions.anchor: Section 'Right User, Right Time, Right Message', p.1
quotes: The goal is to reach individual viewers enough times to push them over a tipping point (called the Minimum Effective Frequency, or MEF) past which brand recognition increases suddenly and dramatically.
Recruit sought a more direct way to identify and reach the maximum number of viewers who could be nurtured to the MEF point within the budget.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of the problem setup and its objective (p.1).

assertions.value: The authors report that the research team learned that controlling the similarity between selected programs improved their ability to cultivate brand recognition in individual viewers, and that the resulting algorithm let Recruit devise a formula to increase the accuracy of view estimations. The paper gives no figures, data set, baseline or method details for this result.
assertions.anchor: Section 'Right User, Right Time, Right Message', p.1
quotes: The research team learned that controlling the similarity between selected programs improved their ability to cultivate brand recognition in individual viewers.
Recruit was also able to devise a formula to increase the accuracy of view estimations.
assertions.certainty_reason: A qualitative result stated in a vendor case story without data or method.
assertions.reader_inference: The page does not say that this similarity control or the view-estimation formula depends on the quantum annealer.

assertions.value: The paper states that combining both methods significantly increased Recruit's ability to identify a target viewer population and engage them with greater efficiency and less expense. No number is given.
assertions.anchor: Section 'Right User, Right Time, Right Message', p.1
quotes: Combining both methods significantly increased their ability to identify a target viewer population and engage them with greater efficiency and less expense.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's description of a customer result; no data in the document.
assertions.reader_inference: The word 'significantly' is not tied to any test or measure in the document.

assertions.value: The paper quotes Kotaro Tanahashi, Machine Learning Engineer at Recruit Communications, as saying that on the TV advertising allocation problem the D-Wave system was used to maximize viewers who recognize a brand and that they got a better result with D-Wave compared to the conventional method. The conventional method is not named and no figure is given.
quotes: we used the D-Wave system to maximize viewers who recognize a brand. We got a better result with D-Wave compared to the conventional method.
assertions.certainty_reason: A testimonial in a vendor document with no data, baseline or metric.
assertions.reader_inference: The testimonial does not say which conventional method, which metric, or by how much.

assertions.value: The paper's figure caption states that recognition of TV ads suddenly increases when the number of ad views exceeds the threshold (the MEF).
quotes: Recognition of TV ads suddenly increases when the number of ad views exceeds the threshold (or MEF)
assertions.certainty_reason: A caption for a chart whose data is not in the text layer and is not sourced.

assertions.value: The paper notes that the project was transferred to Recruit Co.,Ltd.
quotes: Note: This project was transferred to Recruit Co.,Ltd.
assertions.certainty_reason: The document's own footnote on the scope of the attribution (p.1).

assertions.value: The paper states that the machine learning project concerned the accuracy of methods behind marketing technology such as recommendation systems, which compute over a number of features per user, for example gender, browser type, or OS type; and that classical methods such as L1 Regularized Logistic Regression (L1LR) and Feature Selection by Random Forest (RFFS) are only able to deal in approximates due to the high computational cost of addressing these combinatorial problems.
assertions.anchor: Section 'An Expanding Quantum Portfolio: Machine Learning in Marketing', p.2
quotes: L1 Regularized Logistic Regression (L1LR)
Feature Selection by Random Forest (RFFS)
are only able to deal in approximates due to the high computational cost of addressing these combinatorial problems.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's framing of the classical baselines, uncited.

assertions.value: The paper states that Recruit's method, programmed into D-Wave's 2000Q quantum computer, required only 10% of the weak classifiers needed by RFFS to yield consistently better, more accurate results, and that the D-Wave system also showed consistently better results across various data sets and better optimization results overall. The paper gives no data sets, accuracy figures or experimental details.
assertions.anchor: Section 'An Expanding Quantum Portfolio: Machine Learning in Marketing', p.2
quotes: When programmed into D-Wave’s 2000Q™ quantum computer
method required only 10% of the weak classifiers needed by RFFS to yield consistently better, more accurate results.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor-reported empirical result with no data, baseline settings or method in the document.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is against RFFS only, a classical method; the document does not compare against a classical solver of the same selection problem.

assertions.value: The paper states that Recruit explored the optimal order for ranking search results on a hotel reservation website, where separate lists are created for each search segment and updated daily by an algorithm designed to maximize sales, and that Recruit's research aimed to develop an algorithm that accounts for both items' sales scores and diversity within segments.
quotes: separate lists are created for each search segment (area, number of people, price range, etc.) and are updated daily based on an algorithm designed to maximize sales.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own description of the problem setup (p.2).

assertions.value: The authors state that Recruit's results clearly demonstrated that accounting for both sales score and diversity resulted in better performance than considering sales score alone. No figures or experimental details are given.
quotes: accounting for both factors resulted in better performance than considering sales score alone.
assertions.certainty_reason: A qualitative result stated by a vendor without data.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison stated is between two objective choices (sales score plus diversity against sales score alone), not between quantum and classical solvers.

assertions.value: The paper quotes Recruit as saying that with D-Wave they observed a +1% sales uplift in their web services. No baseline, duration, test design or confidence measure is given.
quotes: With D-Wave, we observed a +1% sales uplift in our web services.
assertions.certainty_reason: An unattributed testimonial figure in a vendor document, with no method or baseline.
assertions.reader_inference: The quote is unattributed to a named person, and it does not say that the uplift came from the quantum solver as against the changed objective.

assertions.value: The paper states that Recruit is continuing to explore how D-Wave's quantum system can benefit their business and enhance their Principle of Digital Marketing: Right User, Right Time, Right Message.
quotes: Recruit is continuing to explore how D-Wave
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's statement about a customer's intent.

assertions.value: The document is a 2021 D-Wave Systems case story that ends with an advertisement for the D-Wave Launch program. It contains no methods section, data sets, error bars or references, and it states no limitation of the results it reports.
quotes: the D-Wave Launch program has been designed to help enterprises at every step of their quantum journey, from problem discovery through production implementation.
Sign Up Now To Get Started: www.dwavesys.com/d-wave-launch
© 2021 D-Wave Systems Inc.
assertions.certainty_reason: The absence of methods and limits is the reader's observation of the whole document; the quotes only show its promotional ending.
assertions.reader_inference: Every performance statement in the document is a vendor or customer assertion without a stated method, so none can be checked from this source alone.
